chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about a ship whose occupant is not able to stand: should he perform salat in it while sitting, gesturing, or should he perform sajdah? He said: He should stand, even if he bends his back.

So this narration is to be understood as applying to one who is able to perform salat with a bent back, even if he is not able to stand fully upright. That is permissible according to the order that was detailed previously in the reports, and this is also confirmed by what follows.

key_terms.الرِّوَايَةُ: the narration being interpreted and applied
key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship, the place in which the prayer situation is being discussed
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the reports mentioned earlier that clarify the ruling
key_terms.الْقِيَامِ: standing in salat, the required posture when one is able
key_terms.جَالِسٌ: sitting, an alternative posture when standing is not possible
key_terms.حَنَى ظَهْرَهُ: he bent his back, meaning partial standing with stooping
key_terms.يُومِئُ: gesturing, indicating the prayer movements when full performance is difficult

ai.seo_question: How should a person perform salat on a ship if they cannot stand fully upright?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat in a ship when full standing is difficult. It indicates that if a person can manage some form of standing, even with a bent back, that takes precedence over sitting and gesturing. The closing statement explains the narration in line with earlier reports about the graded order of prayer postures according to one's ability.
